title: Adaptive latency-tier routing with prioritized shedding and failover fencing
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Implement an adaptive multi-region routing policy that enforces per-tenant latency SLOs while preventing cascading failovers. Key features: 1) latency-tier routing that maps requests into latency buckets (fast/target/slow) and prefers regions that keep requests in the lower latency tiers; 2) capacity-aware steering that consumes real-time capacity hints from region capacity manager (Dedicated + Hosted signals) and uses soft-pinning to reduce churn; 3) prioritized load shedding that evicts or degrades lower-priority traffic when SLOs are threatened; 4) failover fencing (new) — a short-lived region lockdown per-customer to avoid flapping between regions during instability.

Why this is different: existing steering policies focus on static geo-pin and simple failover. This ticket implements a combined signal model (latency distribution percentiles + capacity score + historical failover count) and a fencing mechanism that intentionally prevents immediate re-evacuation to the same region for a configurable cooldown. The goal is to improve SLO attainment for P0 tenants during regional incidents while reducing global thrash and protecting tail latencies for priority traffic.
acceptance_criteria: Latency-tier router returns the same routing decision for ~95% of requests under stable load for a given client (no excessive churn)
SLO attainment improvement: for benchmark tenant workloads, 99th-percentile latency reduces by >=20% vs current geo-pin baseline under 2x load
Circuit-breaker integration: region-level CB trips when error-rate > 5% or avg latency > configured fail_threshold for 30s; subsequent routing respects CB state
Prioritized shedding: when capacity score < threshold, low-priority requests (labels) are shed first and not routed to affected regions
Failover fencing: after automated failover, the evicted region is marked fenced for that tenant for configurable cooldown (default 5 minutes) and UI exposes fencing state
Automated canary: rollout to 5% of tenants with observability dashboards and alerting configured
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Simulation (this sprint): implement router in staging, feed synthetic latency/capacity traces, validate decision stability
Phase 1 - Canary (runtime-1.22 beta): enable for 5% low-risk tenants, monitor SLOs, error budgets, and routing churn for 48h
Phase 2 - Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 50% over 2 weeks with automatic rollback on high error-rate or >10% increase in SLO violations
Phase 3 - Global: full clusterwide enable with migration playbook and runbook published
metrics: Routing churn rate per tenant (decisions changed within 60s) - target < 5%
Error-rate and circuit-breaker trips per region
Number of fences created per tenant per hour and average fence duration
Capacity hint utilization ratio (allocated vs used)
notes: Design decision: use quantile-based latency tiers (p50/p90/p99) sampled at request-level with 10s sliding window to avoid noisy single-sample flips
We will require a light-weight per-tenant routing state (sticky hint + fence timestamp) in the routing service; persisted for 1h TTL
Interaction with Dedicated: capacity hints will be fetched from dedicated-control plane (new API) and normalized into a 0-1 capacity score
Failover fencing aims to reduce 'ping-pong' by adding an explicit cooldown; cooldown is tenant-configurable and will be exposed through Console rollouts
Security: no PII is stored in the routing state. Security review not required for initial implementation but product may request for enterprise features
